use_case_summary: Customer is building in-product assistant and semantic search for their analytics SaaS. High concurrent chat volume during product events + nightly batch embedding of docs. Priority: predictable latency for chat (p95) and deterministic monthly cost for forecasting.
requirements_summary:
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for short chat prompts (user-facing) during normal ops; tolerate 400ms during event bursts.
- Throughput: steady-state ~150 qps chat tokens, burst spikes up to 600 qps for 10-30 min events.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market finance team needs committed spend predictability, overage should not exceed 1.5x committed unit price.
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2, audit logs forwarded to SIEM, KMS for key management, EU data residency for EU customers.
- Operational: Rollout window for new model versions must support canary and instant fallback to prior variant.
pricing_negotiation_summary:
Negotiation points and current positions:
- Redwood proposal A (starter): 6-month Dedicated commit = 2 x small GPU pools (baseline throughput 200 qps), monthly commit $18k, burst to 400 qps included for 10% of minutes, overage billed at 1.8x unit rate.
- Redwood proposal B (preferred): 12-month commit = 3 x small GPU pools, monthly commit $30k, burst allowance 2x baseline for up to 8% of time, overage at 1.5x. Includes 30-day ramp credits in months 1-2.
- Customer counter: Wants 9-month with burst 2x and overage cap 1.25x; requests guaranteed 90-day ramp schedule with credits if capacity not reached.
- SE note: measuring cost in committed GPU-hours vs token units; recommended optimize tuning (quant, batch, cache) to reduce effective cost by ~20% within POC.
- Current ask from Procurement: explicit formula for burst pricing, clarification on how autoscale interacts with committed capacity, and a 60-day break clause tied to SLA misses.
